review_candidates.description: About The Job Job summary Discover a career in your hands at HMRC. Whether you're seeking purpose, growth, or a workplace that gives you a true sense of belonging, hear from some of our employees as they share their story about what it's really like to work at HMRC. Visit our YouTube channel to watch the full series and come and discover your potential. Enterprise Integration Services (EIS) are at the heart of the HMRC Chief Digital Information Officer (CDIO) group. EIS manage HMRC's core integration services, taking care of over a billion transactions every year and connecting hundreds of HMRC services and platforms. EIS provide platforms for delivering Application Programming Interface (API) access and File Transfer (FT) capability to HMRC Systems. We provide artefacts and support for API customers (software developers and Other Government Departments) to build and manage authorised software that seamlessly integrates with HMRC digital services. We use modern open-source products and work in an Agile way to deliver flexible, effective integration solutions. We are also transforming our legacy services into cloud-based platforms. Job Description The Platform Operations Technical Manager will provide senior technical leadership across DevOps and production support teams responsible for critical live services. The role will ensure the team has the technical capability, operational processes and cross-platform knowledge required to maintain secure, reliable and resilient services. The postholder will act as the senior technical escalation point for complex incidents, provide assurance for releases and changes, improve monitoring and automation, and drive continuous improvement across the platform estate. You will lead a team of DevOps Engineers. You will have a record of using your own initiative to good effect and making fact-based decisions on service management and support issues. You will be a credible, influential, and encouraging team-player. You will also be proactive, a confident communicator with good people skills and a dedication to continuous improvement in self and others. This role involves being On-call. EIS has a Departmental Working Agreement whereby the out of hours working are Monday to Friday 6pm to 8am and Saturday and Sunday all day. This is normally 1 week in every 4 weeks. This is an exciting opportunity for someone with recent experience in a similar role who enjoys working in a dynamic, multifaceted environment. What makes EIS Live Services particularly engaging is the chance to lead within a high-profile, fast-paced setting where operational resilience is essential. The role brings together service stability, governance, supplier management and continuous improvement, supporting critical services that the business depends on every day. It is both challenging and rewarding, requiring strong collaboration, confident decision-making and a consistent focus on ensuring services remain safe, resilient and effective. Person specification Responsibilities The successful candidate will be an experienced technical leader with a strong background in DevOps, production support and the operation of critical live services. You will be able to lead and develop a team of DevOps Engineers, make evidence-based decisions and provide confident technical leadership within a complex, fast-paced environment. Strong technical leadership skills, with experience of managing, coaching and mentoring DevOps Engineers or other technical specialists. Experience of supporting secure, reliable and resilient live services across complex technology platforms. Strong knowledge of IT service management practices, including incident, problem, change, release, risk and service continuity management. Experience of acting as a senior technical escalation point during complex incidents, supporting effective service recovery and identifying improvements. Experience of providing technical assurance for releases, changes and platform improvements, ensuring risks and service impacts are understood and effectively managed. Experience of improving monitoring, alerting, automation and operational processes to increase service reliability and reduce manual effort. Ability to use performance data, technical evidence and service insights to make informed decisions and drive continuous improvement. Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to work collaboratively and influence technical teams, suppliers and senior stakeholders. Experience of managing service performance across multiple platforms and working effectively within a multi-supplier environment. A proactive and collaborative leadership style, with the confidence to use initiative, manage competing priorities and remain calm under pressure. Experience supporting early mission concept development, architecture studies, or Phase A/B spacecraft programs. Background in spacecraft hardware development through design reviews, integration and test activities, requirements management, or operational support. Familiarity with thermal analysis methodologies and tools, including coordination with thermal engineering teams during spacecraft development. Experience with deployable systems, mechanisms, robotics, capture systems, or other moving aerospace hardware. Knowledge of launch vehicle integration constraints, payload accommodations, and mission interface requirements. Experience with mass properties tracking, configuration management, and engineering data control processes.
